name: GA-08
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Austin Scott seeking re-election with large financial edge
Democratic challenger Kelly Esti has raised only ~$19K with minimal cash
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~97%
model.rationale: Austin Scott is an entrenched incumbent in a district that leans Republican by 15 points, and he holds an overwhelming fundraising advantage over a barely funded challenger. Markets and fundamentals both point to a decisive Republican win with little evidence suggesting a competitive race.
model.watch: A major late-breaking scandal or unexpected outside spending surge could narrow the margin, but no such signs are present.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Georgia's 8th District is a solidly Republican seat in rural and central Georgia, with a partisan lean of about 15 points toward the GOP. Austin Scott has held the seat since 2011 and is running again after easily securing renomination.

Scott enters the general election with roughly $1.1 million raised and $1.3 million on hand, while Democratic challenger Kelly Esti has raised under $20,000 and reports minimal cash. No public polls or expert ratings track the race, and prediction markets give Scott about a 97% chance of winning. The fundamentals, money gap, and district lean all point to a comfortable Republican victory, with the only uncertainty being the exact size of the margin.
